# E170 PRE-REGISTRATION - memory extraction, three local models (2026-11-21)

## In plain English

A memory system for an assistant reads conversations and writes down what it learned about the person: where they
are based, what they pay, which tools they use, what was decided. Doing that every night is many small, dull jobs,
so it is worth running on a local model if one is good enough.

Someone in the Strix Halo community reported that a small model, Inkling Mini, beats our production model at
exactly this work, and that Hy-Memory (built for it) was the best local model before that. This test checks that
claim on our machine, with traps a memory system must not fall for: a colleague's details, a "we might move to...",
a suggestion the person turned down, and a mistake the person corrects mid-sentence.

The winner becomes the model for a nightly job that proposes memory entries for the owner to accept (owner
2026-11-21: "Run E170 first, then pick").

## Why (owner 2026-11-21)

Owner chose "Run E170 first, then pick" for the extraction job's model, with proposals landing as SparkContext
suggestions. The community report is one person's Honcho setup with their own scoring; this is ours, mechanical and
pre-registered.

## Bank

`spikes/memory-tasks/bank.json`, 50 tasks, every person and business invented, ground truth by construction.

- **Extract X01-X30:** a conversation in, facts about the user out, each `confirmed` or `suggestion`, from 9 fixed
  keys. Each task plants 5 true facts, one self-correction (only the corrected value is right), a colleague's fact
  and a hypothetical on keys the user has stated, and an assistant suggestion that is rejected (odd tasks) or left at
  "maybe" (even tasks; allowed only with status `suggestion`).
- **Update U01-U20:** stored memory (6 keys) plus a conversation with two real changes, one restatement, one new fact
  and one trap on an unchanged key; the full updated memory out.

Limits stated now: the conversations are templated and short (about 17 turns), so this measures following the rules
of memory-keeping on clear text, not reading long or messy real conversations. A model that does well here has passed
a floor, not proved itself on real captures.

## Arms

| arm | model | engine | how called |
|---|---|---|---|
| F | production Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (community template) | Halogen, live production | model-guard 127.0.0.1:8402, `local_smart`, no effort sent = the live default `low` |
| I | Inkling-2-Mini (thinkingmachines, rev `ed40e7da`), converted by us to GGUF Q8_0 | llama.cpp `e412c6f46` (2026-11-21), Vulkan | sparkbench llama-server, `-c 16384 -np 1` |
| H | Hy-Memory-30B-A3B Q8_0 (tencent official GGUF, rev `38e10a37`) | same build | same |

All arms: one user message, temperature 0, one sample, `max_tokens` 16,384, each model's own chat template. Arms run
one at a time; I and H run on a sparkbench llama-server alongside live production, so wall times are indicative,
not a speed benchmark (Rule 9 and Rule 10 are therefore out of scope; no speed claim will be made). Production's
default effort is checked with `/opt/sparkrouter/ops/halogen_effort_check.py` before and after arm F.

## Fields

`results/e170/score.json`, per arm:

- `extract.f1`, `extract.precision`, `extract.recall`: confirmed (key, value) facts against the planted truth, micro
  over 30 tasks (150 true facts).
- `extract.trust_errors` = `stale + colleague + hypothetical + rejected + promoted`: wrong values recorded as
  confirmed facts about the user (max 120 trap opportunities plus 15 promotable suggestions).
- `extract.valid`: replies that parsed as the requested JSON.
- `update.exact`: tasks whose whole returned memory equals the truth (of 20). `update.stale_kept`,
  `update.unchanged_lost`, `update.trap_hits`.
- `wall_s_median`: indicative only.

## Predictions

| | prediction | field |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | The bank is not too easy to separate: at least one arm scores below 0.95 | `extract.f1` |
| P2 | The community ranking does not reproduce: neither I nor H beats F by 0.05 or more | `extract.f1(I) - extract.f1(F)` and `(H) - (F)`, each `< 0.05` |
| P3 | Production makes the fewest trust errors | `extract.trust_errors(F) <= min(I, H)` |
| P4 | Every arm returns valid JSON on at least 28 of 30 extract tasks | `extract.valid` |
| P5 | Production gets the most whole-memory updates exactly right | `update.exact(F) >= max(I, H)` |

## Decision rule (stated now)

The nightly job's model is the arm with the highest `extract.f1` among arms whose `extract.trust_errors` is no higher
than production's. Within 0.03 F1 of each other, the faster arm (`wall_s_median`) wins, because the job runs beside
production. If no arm passes 0.85 F1, no model is chosen and the job is not built on this evidence.

## Things that would void a result

- An engine fault rather than a model result: before scoring arm I, I read five of its raw replies by hand; Inkling
  support in llama.cpp was merged on 2026-11-20 (`29b52d398`). A conversion or template defect makes arm I void, not
  a loss, and is reported as such.
- Any change to the bank, prompts or grader after the first model call voids the comparison unless declared as an
  amendment here before the affected runs.
